Rashi on Niddah 17a:10:2.hebrew: בעלי ראתן - חלשים יותר מדאי, שיש להם שרץ במוחם, כדאמר בכתובות:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:10:2.english: Those afflicted with ra'atan - Exceedingly weak, for they have an insect in their brain, as [the Gemara] says in Ketubot.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:12:1.english: A Torah scholar - Because he knows how to conduct himself modestly.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:14:1.hebrew: אף על פי שאמרו המשמש מטתו כו' - כדאיתא בברייתא דלעיל בריש שמעתין, ומסקנא: או תשמש לאור הנר. אלמא מגונה הוא דהוי, אבל איסורא ליכא, מדקתני: או תשמש. והשתא ליכא למימר תבדוק, דא"כ מאי אע"פ שאמרו כו':
Rashi on Niddah 17a:14:1.english: Even though they said: One who engages in intercourse, etc. - As is stated in the baraita above, at the beginning of our discussion [16b], and its conclusion [is]: "Or she may engage in intercourse by the light of a lamp." Evidently, it is [merely] repulsive, but there is no [actual] prohibition, since it teaches: "Or she may engage in intercourse." And now, one cannot say [that it means] "she may examine," for if so, what is [the meaning of]: "Even though they said," etc.?

Rashi on Niddah 17a:14:2.hebrew: אימא הבודק מטתו לאור הנר כו' - משום דלא מיבדיק שפיר, אפ"ה או תביא שני עדים לכל תשמיש, או תבדוק לאור הנר:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:14:2.english: Say: One who examines his bed by the light of a lamp, etc. - Because it is not examined well. Even so, either she must bring two examination cloths for each act of intercourse, or she must examine by the light of a lamp.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:15:1.hebrew: מילא פרהבא - קוטו"ן. מתוך שהוא לבן, נראית בו טיפה כחרדל. לישנא אחרינא: צמר נקי ורך:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:15:1.english: Wool of Parhava - Cotton. Since it is white, a drop [as small] as a mustard seed is visible on it. Another version: Clean and soft wool.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:16:1.hebrew: ומזכירין חכמים אותן לשבח - בתמיה: נהי אי הוה מותר בעלמא, הוה תמיה לן, וכ"ש שמזכירין לשבח! ומה הוא שבחן:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:16:1.english: And the Sages mention them for praise - [This is said] as a question: Granted, even if it were permitted in general, it would be astonishing to us, and all the more so that they mention [them] for praise! And what is their praise?

Rashi on Niddah 17a:16:2.hebrew: אונס שינה - מתוך שהוא נאנס בשינה, אינו מתאווה לה כל כך, ומשמש לקיום מצות עונה בעלמא או לרצותה, ולבו קץ בה. והוא מבני תשע מדות דאמרו בנדרי' (דף כ:):
Rashi on Niddah 17a:16:2.english: The compulsion of sleep - Since he is overcome by sleep, he does not desire her so much, and engages in intercourse merely to fulfill the mitzvah of onah [conjugal rights] or to appease her, while his heart is repulsed by her. And this is among the 'children of nine traits' that they stated in Nedarim (page 20b).

Rashi on Niddah 17a:17:2.english: That when I was there - In the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:17:3.english: On Shabbat eves - The time of the conjugal obligation of the abstinent and Torah scholars is from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:18:1.english: Worn-out linen garments - Worn-out garments of linen.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:18:2.hebrew: ולא בפשתן - שאינו לבן, ואין דם ניכר יפה אלא בעד לבן:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:18:2.english: Nor with flax - Because it is not white, and blood is not clearly discernible except on a white cloth.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:19:1.english: Worn-out [garments] - [They are] whiter than the new ones.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:20:1.english: If one designated it, etc. - For it is closer to being a liquid than food.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:1.hebrew: לא נטמא כו' - דאינו חבור, אלא כל קורט בפני עצמו חשוב, ואינו טמא אלא מקום מגע טומאה:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:1.english: It did not become impure, etc. - For it is not a connected unit, but rather each particle is considered on its own, and only the place of contact with the impurity is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:2.hebrew: נטהר מקצתו - כגון חישב עליו למשקה ונטמא טומאת משקין, סלקא ליה השקה במקוה כשאר מים. ולא משום טבילה, דאין אוכל ומשקה נטהרין במקוה, דלא כתיב טבילה אלא באדם וכלי. אבל יין ולא שום משקה אין להם טהרה אלא מים, ומשום זריעה, דכי משיק להו הוו להו חבור מים שבכלי עם מי המקוה, ובטילו להו גבייהו. כדתנן (תרומות פ"ט מ"ז): שתילי תרומה שנטמאו ושתלן טהרו מלטמא, אלמא מטהרא להו זריעה, ומים במים זו היא זריעתן:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:2.english: Part of it was purified - For example, where one designated it for drink and it became defiled with the impurity of liquids, contact [hashakah] in a mikveh is effective for it, just like other water. And [this is] not because of immersion, for food and drink are not purified in a mikveh, as immersion is written only regarding a person and vessels. However, neither wine nor any other liquid has purification, except water, and [even that is] because of sowing [zeri'ah]. For when one brings them into contact, the water in the vessel forms a connection with the water of the mikveh, and they become nullified to them. As we learned in a mishna (Terumot 9:7): "Seedlings of terumah that became impure and one planted them, they are purified from imparting impurity." Evidently, sowing purifies them; and [bringing] water into water, this is its sowing.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:3.english: Part of it was purified - Where the water [of the mikveh] touched only at the mouth of the vessel.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:4.hebrew: נטהר כולו - ומדקתני נטהר כולו, מכלל דטמא כולו, והיכי משכחת לה דנגעה טומאה בכולו:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:21:4.english: All of it is purified - And since [the baraita] teaches, "All of it is purified," it implies that all of it was impure. And how can you find [a case] where ritual impurity touched all of it?

Rashi on Niddah 17a:23:1.english: That one passed it - [Namely,] the snow.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:23:2.hebrew: על אויר תנור - ושרץ בתוכו, דנטמא מאויר כלי חרס:
Rashi on Niddah 17a:23:2.english: Over the airspace of an oven - And a creeping animal is inside it, so that [the snow] is rendered impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:23:3.english: For the Torah testified - [As the verse states:] "Whatever is in it shall be impure" (Leviticus 11:33).

Rashi on Niddah 17a:5:2.english: Their roots - The hairs at the head of the garlic and the onion.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:7:1.english: A spirit of impurity - Like the practice of the jesters who are called gramantier [conjurers], who deceive the eyes.

Rashi on Niddah 17a:9:1.english: Pious - [This level is] superior to [that of] a righteous person. When one buries them, there is reason to be concerned that they will become uncovered again.

Tosafot on Niddah 17a:16:1.hebrew: אימא בודקין מטותיהן ביום - ולכן מזכירין לשבח, דאע"ג דאמרו ב"ש צריכה ב' עדים על כל תשמיש ותשמיש, ולב"ה דיה בב' עדים כל הלילה ומעיינא בהו למחר; מ"מ מודו, דאם רוצה לעיין בלילה לאור הנר, הרשות בידה:
Tosafot on Niddah 17a:16:1.english: Say: They examine their beds by day - And therefore they are mentioned for praise, for even though Beit Shammai said [that] she requires two examination cloths for each and every act of intercourse, and according to Beit Hillel two examination cloths suffice for her for the entire night and she examines them the next day; nevertheless, they agree that if she wishes to examine [them] at night by the light of a lamp, she is permitted to do so.

Tosafot on Niddah 17a:19:1.hebrew: הא בחדתי הא בשחקי - תימה, דבפ"ק דשבועות (דף ו:) גבי שאת כצמר לבן, שניה לה כקרום ביצה, ומפרש כמו גלימא דכיתנא ושחקיה, משמע שהחדש לבן מן הישן. וי"ל, דהתם בגלימא שאין רגילות לכבס, והכא בחלוק וכיוצא בו שמכבסין תדיר. ועוד י"ל, דהתם לענין חשיבות מיירי, כי הנך דלעיל, כגון שבור מלכא וריש גלותא:
Tosafot on Niddah 17a:19:1.english: This is regarding new [garments], that is regarding worn-out [ones] - It is puzzling, for in the first chapter of Shevuot (6b), regarding [the mishna]: "A se'et is like white wool, [and] secondary to it is [like] an egg membrane," and [the Gemara] explains: "like a linen cloak and its worn-out [counterpart]" — which implies that the new is whiter than the old! And one can say that there [in Shevuot, it is speaking] of a cloak, which it is not customary to launder; but here [in Niddah, it is speaking] of a tunic and the like, which they launder frequently. And furthermore, one can say that there it is dealing with the matter of importance, like those [analogies mentioned] above, such as King Shapur and the Exilarch.

Tosafot on Niddah 17a:9:1.hebrew: שורפן חסיד - דליכא למיחש שמא יתגלו. ובערוך [ערך שלש] פירש ששרפת צפורן מזקת לאדם, וכן כל דבר הבא מן האדם, כדאמר בס"פ כלל גדול (שבת דף עה:) גבי דם הנדה: איידי דחלשא לא מצנעה לשונרא. ולכך הוא חסיד, שמחמיר לשורפן אע"ג שמזיק לו:
Tosafot on Niddah 17a:9:1.english: One who burns them is pious - For there is no concern lest they become uncovered. And in the Arukh [entry shalash], he explained that burning a fingernail harms a person, and so too anything that comes from a person, as [the Gemara] says at the end of the chapter "Klal Gadol" (Shabbat 75b) regarding the blood of a niddah: "Since she becomes weak, she does not save it for a cat." And therefore he is [called] pious, for he is stringent to burn them even though it harms him.
